cards.title: Layers: staging → processed → curated
cards.text: Raw data lands in staging unchanged, is cleaned and conformed in processed, and is shaped for consumers in curated. Each layer is a contract: readers of curated never reach back into staging, and every artifact belongs to exactly one layer.

cards.title: Lineage: know where every table comes from
cards.text: Every table should have a known producer and known inputs. With lineage you can answer what breaks if a source changes and where a wrong number came from. A table nobody can trace is a table nobody can safely change.

cards.title: Idempotence: a rerun gives the same result
cards.text: A job that fails halfway will be rerun. Overwrite, partition overwrite or merge on a key leave the same result after a rerun; a blind append duplicates rows. Pick the write mode so that running twice is harmless.

cards.title: Quality gates between layers
cards.text: Check data where it crosses a layer boundary: keys unique, required columns filled, volumes plausible. A failed check stops or quarantines the load instead of passing bad rows on to the next layer and to reports.

cards.title: Slowly changing dimensions
cards.text: When a customer moves or a product is renamed, decide per attribute whether history matters. Type 1 overwrites; type 2 keeps a dated row per version, through snapshots or a merge on the dimension key. Not deciding silently loses history.

cards.title: Partitioning large tables
cards.text: Partition big tables on the column most queries and loads filter on, usually a date. Readers then skip whole folders and reloads replace one partition. Too many small partitions cost more than none.
